case_name: O.P. Garg and Others v State of Uttar Pradesh and Others
facts: The service was initially governed by statutory rules called the Uttar Pradesh Higher Judicial Service Rules, 1953 (hereinafter called '1953 rules').
This members of the service promoted under the 1953 rules were designated as Civil and Sessions Judges.
On May 8, 1974 the Uttar Pradesh Higher Judicial Service (abolition of cadre of the Civil and Sessions Judges) Rules, 1974 (hereinafter called ' 1974 rules ') came into force.
The relevant rules, 5, 6, 8 and 26 are reproduced hereinafter:
Statement of facts filed by the High Court shows that on April 5, 1975, when the 1975 Rules came into force, there were 229 permanent and 7 temporary (total 236) posts in the service.
P.K. Dixit and 7 other promotee officers filed two writ petitions u/art. 32 of the Constitution of India challenging the seniority assigned to them on two grounds.
The promotes claim that the judgment in Dixit case is wholly in their favour on the first point.
Objections were invited against the tentative seniority list and thereafter the High Court constituted a five-Judge committee to finalise the list.
petitioner_arguments: All the posts, existing on April 5, 1975 when the 1975 Rules came into force should be deemed to have been filled by the officers holding the designation of Additional District and Sessions Judges on that date.
The promotees were entitled to the seniority from the date of their actual continuous officiation and not by limiting they said period to three years preceding the date of confirmation.
respondent_arguments: The contention of the promotees was rejected and their claim was confined to the number of posts as provided in First Proviso to rule 8(2) of the 1975 Rules.
The direct recruits, however, contest the said claim and assert that the judgment in Dixit case is not wholly in favour of the promotes.
holding: The final seniority list was issued on August 25, 1988.
